service: Implantable pulmonary artery pressure sensor (IPAPS) for heart failure management
notes: All cases satisfy the physician criteria (B.2) and the CED study requirement unless stated. Study-protocol design criteria (B.3 a-f) are study-level and not tested.

criteria.text: Furnished according to an FDA market-authorized indication
criteria.span: Implantation of an IPAPS is covered for HF management when furnished according to a Food and Drug Administration (FDA) market-authorized indication

criteria.text: Chronic HF >= 3 months and NYHA class II or III within the past 30 days, regardless of LVEF
criteria.span: Diagnosis of chronic HF of at least 3 months duration and in New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional Class II or III within the past 30 days, prior to PAPS implantation, regardless of left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF).

criteria.text: HF hospitalization or urgent IV-diuretic visit within 12 months, or elevated natriuretic peptides within 30 days
criteria.span: History of HF hospitalization or urgent HF visit (emergency room (ER) or other outpatient (OP) visit requiring intravenous (IV) diuretic therapy) within the past 12 months, or elevated natriuretic peptides within the past 30 days.

criteria.text: On GDMT for at least 3 months
criteria.span: On guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) for at least 3 months with the goal of achieving optimal or maximally-tolerated GDMT prior to PAPS implantation.

criteria.text: Evaluated for (and received if appropriate) ICD/CRT-P/CRT-D; any such device implanted >= 3 months before
criteria.span: Evaluated for, and received if appropriate, an implantable cardioverter defibrillator (ICD), cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT)-Pacemaker (CRT-P), or CRT-Defibrillator (CRT-D). Implantation of the device must occur at least 3 months prior to PAPS implantation.

criteria.text: No major cardiovascular event within the last 3 months
criteria.span: No major cardiovascular event (e.g., unstable angina, myocardial infarction, percutaneous coronary intervention, open heart surgery, or stroke) within the last 3 months prior to PAPS implantation.

criteria.text: Access to reliable connectivity for daily data transmission
criteria.span: Have access to reliable connectivity to ensure daily collection and submission of IPAPS data.

criteria.text: Implantation not during a hospital admission for an acute HF episode
criteria.span: Must not have PAPS implantation occur during a hospital admission for an acute HF episode.

criteria.text: Referring/managing physician is a cardiologist with HF training; implanter trained in PA catheterization
criteria.span: Physicians referring Medicare patients and managing them post implantation must be cardiologists with training and experience in HF management.

criteria.text: Furnished in a CMS-approved CED study; not covered outside one
criteria.span: IPAPS for HF management is not covered for patients outside of a CMS-approved study.

cases.note: All patient criteria met. Preserved LVEF and stage 4 CKD are not exclusions ('regardless of LVEF'; CKD is only a study subgroup).
cases.vignette: 79-year-old woman with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (LVEF 58% by echocardiography) diagnosed 3 years ago, and stage 4 chronic kidney disease. She was NYHA class III at a clinic visit 12 days ago. She was hospitalized for acute decompensated heart failure 5 months ago. She has been on guideline-directed medical therapy, titrated to maximally tolerated doses, for over 2 years. She was evaluated for ICD and CRT; neither is indicated. No myocardial infarction, unstable angina, coronary intervention, cardiac surgery, or stroke in the past year. She has home broadband and cellular service and has demonstrated daily transmission with the study's home unit. Implantation is scheduled as an elective outpatient procedure. The referring and post-implant managing physician is a cardiologist with training and experience in heart failure management, and the implanting interventional cardiologist has training and experience in pulmonary arterial catheterization and intervention. The sensor is an FDA market-authorized IPAPS to be implanted for its authorized indication. The patient is enrolled in a CMS-approved CED study of IPAPS.

cases.note: Boundaries: HF diagnosed and GDMT started exactly 3 months before implant; no HF hospitalization, but elevated NT-proBNP 25 days ago satisfies the 'or' branch.
